title: Lab: size the KV cache
summary: Compute the attention state a serving system must hold per token, per sequence and per batch.

blocks.md:
During generation each layer keeps a key and a value vector for every past token so it never recomputes them. The cache size is

$$M_{KV} = 2 \cdot L \cdot H_{kv} \cdot d_h \cdot T \cdot B \cdot b$$

layers, KV heads, head dimension, tokens, concurrent sequences and bytes per value. Unlike the weights, it grows with every token and every user.

steps.why: Key and value, every layer, every KV head.
Before a single weight is loaded.

challenge.md: Without grouped-query attention the model would keep **32 KV heads**. What would the whole batch's cache be, in GB?
challenge.hint: Four times as many KV heads.
challenge.explanation: 4 × 17.18 GB ≈ 68.7 GB: almost a whole 80 GB accelerator for the cache alone. Sharing KV heads is one of the main levers serving has.

blocks.title: KV cache calculator
blocks.md: Complete `kv_bytes`, then use `max_sequences` to see how many 8K conversations fit beside 14 GB of weights on an 80 GB accelerator.
blocks.code:
def kv_bytes(layers, kv_heads, head_dim, tokens, batch=1, bytes_per=2):
    # TODO
    return None


def max_sequences(free_gb, tokens, **model):
    per_seq = kv_bytes(tokens=tokens, **model)
    return int(free_gb * 1e9 // per_seq) if per_seq else None


model = dict(layers=32, kv_heads=8, head_dim=128)
print(kv_bytes(tokens=1, **model), 'bytes per token')
print(max_sequences(80 - 14, 8192, **model), 'sequences of 8K tokens')
blocks.check:
assert kv_bytes(32, 8, 128, 1) == 131072
assert kv_bytes(32, 8, 128, 8192, batch=16) == 17179869184
assert max_sequences(66, 8192, layers=32, kv_heads=8, head_dim=128) == 61
blocks.hint: `2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * tokens * batch * bytes_per`.

questions.q: Same model, one sequence of 128K (131,072) tokens. How many GB of KV cache (1 decimal)?
questions.explanation: 131,072² B ≈ 17.2 GB for one long conversation: as much as a batch of sixteen 8K ones.

questions.q: Storing the cache in fp8 instead of bf16 does what?
options: Halves the cache, so twice as many sequences fit
Removes the need for a cache
questions.hint: Bytes per value goes from 2 to 1.
questions.explanation: Every term but b stays the same, so memory halves. The cost is a small accuracy risk that has to be evaluated.

points: KV cache = 2 · layers · KV heads · head dim · tokens · batch · bytes.
It grows with context length and concurrency, so it caps how many users fit.
Levers: fewer KV heads (GQA), lower precision, paging and prefix sharing.
